card.name: Linking words before treatment-decision clauses
card.fires_on: Small linking words (who, to, should, have) that open a clause about what to do for a patient group or about stopping treatment. Seen in label text on retreatment, nursing infants and discontinuation.

modes.label: Who after patient group
modes.description: The word who or have right after patients or a condition, introducing a qualifying clause.
modes.example: retreatment may be considered for patients with multiple myeloma<< who>> had previously responded to treatment with Bort

modes.label: To after whether (nursing)
modes.description: The word to after a decision should be made whether, before discontinue nursing or the drug.
modes.example: a decision should be made whether<< to>> discontinue nursing or to discontinue the

modes.label: Should after a stopping subject
modes.description: The word should after a subject who stops or starts a therapy, before a monitoring or action instruction.
modes.example: Patients with HIV-1 and HBV who discontinue ODEFSEY<< should>> be closely monitored with both clinical and laboratory

card.writes: It seems to add little that is readable; the promoted and suppressed tokens are mostly mixed-language and unrelated.
card.plain: It fires on the small connecting word that leads into a clause saying what applies to a certain group of patients or what to do about stopping a drug.
